solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retiring gentleman given the sack? That's rubbish

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the pieces given are read from the end to the start

parts.note: SIR is the title of a gentleman or knight
to hit the sack is to go to bed, so the sack means bed

explanation.surface: A man has been fired, and someone dismisses him as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns SIRBED round as a whole. 'Given the sack' looks like dismissal, but the sack here is a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scattered remains and litter are both called rubbish.

clue.text: Police officers plot to kill

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a plot of land is a patch

explanation.surface: Detectives uncover a conspiracy to murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme, but it is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone off for good, in the sense of execute or kill.

clue.text: Make a huge effort getting university blokes' party into bar

indicators.note: into means the party pieces go inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar means except, which is but
a stag is a party for men before a wedding

explanation.surface: Students make a big effort to get their stag party into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but means except, giving BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to strain so hard you might burst, meaning to try extremely hard.

clue.text: One group of men serving Queen and country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the RAN is the Royal Australian Navy, which served the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier serves his monarch and his nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Middle East, formerly called Persia.

clue.text: Daughter is to wed — that's involved having a couple of parties

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A father announces his daughter's wedding, noting the complications of bringing two families together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges DISTOWED, which is D followed by IS, TO and WED.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest or argument with a couple of parties has two opposing camps.

clue.text: Generous with description of Polo?

parts.note: a Polo is a British mint sweet with a hole in its middle, so it is hole-hearted

explanation.surface: A writer looks for a generous way to describe Marco Polo or the game of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a British ring-shaped peppermint advertised as the mint with the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving fully and sincerely, without holding back, as a generous person does.

clue.text: To start new domestic life, he put pants in to soak

indicators.note: in means the mixed letters go inside the word for soak

parts.note: to souse is to drench or soak

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A newlywed man puts his underpants in to soak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' rearranges HEPUT into ETUPH, placed 'in' SOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to establish a home of one's own, often on marrying.

clue.text: One who composed for keyboard

definitions.meaning: the Czech composer Antonin of that name wrote the New World Symphony
a simplified keyboard layout bearing that name is an alternative to QWERTY

explanation.surface: A composer who wrote keyboard music.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the surname: the Czech composer and August, inventor of a typing layout.

clue.text: Pastry cook's creation has a new filling

indicators.note: filling means the letters go inside the dish

parts.note: a dish is what a cook creates

explanation.surface: A cook's pastry has a fresh filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet flaky breakfast pastry named after Denmark.

clue.text: Picked up small bag for excursion

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for a small bag is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sachet is a small sealed bag or packet

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a little bag before heading off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like lifting the bag, but it signals a sound-alike: sachet is pronounced like the word for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefly American usage: a jaunt or outing, a little trip out.

clue.text: Old officer stops Tom playing chicken

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the old officer is put inside the word for Tom

parts.note: tom is British slang for a prostitute, a pro
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
a performer who is playing is on

explanation.surface: A retired officer prevents Tom from playing chicken, the dare game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a name: in British slang a tom is a prostitute, giving PRO, which 'stops' (plugs) with OLT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a chicken is a coward, and an utter coward is called this.

clue.text: Providing only a little bread, dashed in, up for food

indicators.note: dashed means smashed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Someone dashes in and gets up for a meal that offers little bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, and 'dashed' rearranges INUPFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, so earning little of it means making no profit.

clue.text: Amateur weightlifter's said to be a hero!

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words before it are taken by their sound

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for amateur; a jack lifts heavy weights such as cars, so weightlifters are jacks

explanation.surface: An amateur weightlifter is hailed as a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: A JACKS sounds like the hero's name; 'weightlifter' is not an athlete but a car jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is one of the Greek heroes of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Makes light of pal's extremely nasty, rude snarling

indicators.note: snarling means tangling, so these letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: pal's is read as the plural pals, giving its four letters

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of nasty

explanation.surface: Someone downplays a friend's very rude, aggressive snarling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes NY from nasty; 'snarling' (tangling, not growling) mixes PALS, NY and RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make light of something is to treat it as less important than it is.

clue.text: Navigate river to find Dickens character

parts.note: to steer is to navigate
the Forth is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Steering down a river, you meet someone from a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: James Steerforth is David Copperfield's charming but faithless friend in the novel.

clue.text: Singer's withdrawn single after short time in token resistance

indicators.note: in tells us the time and the single are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a counter is a token used in board games
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: after places the single behind the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for single is read backwards

parts.note: one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A singer has backed out of a single after only a brief, token show of resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' and 'after' build TENO, which goes 'in' the token-plus-resistance pair. 'Singer's' is the definition with a link 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A male singer whose voice is in the alto range, above the tenor.

clue.text: No support for Brazil's heroes? Lots and lots!

indicators.note: no means without, so the support garment is removed from the country's name

parts.note: the country's name, the possessive adding no letter
a bra is a supporting garment
brave heroes are called lions

explanation.surface: Brazil's sporting heroes get no support, a great many complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No support' takes BRA from BRAZIL, leaving ZIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an indefinitely huge number.

clue.text: Pilot, say, keeping height up after he had to fly low

indicators.note: after places the reversed pieces behind the contraction of he had

parts.note: he had contracts to he'd

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, backwards
keeping means holding, so height goes inside

parts.note: PO is a Pilot Officer, an RAF rank
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A pilot keeps his altitude up after deciding to fly low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts H in POEG; 'up' reverses POHEG to GEHOP, placed 'after' HED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly very low, as if hopping over hedges, as crop-sprayers do.

clue.text: Base car rental around southern part of England

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a bed of gravel

indicators.note: around means the car rental is placed about the letter for southern

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car
hire is renting

explanation.surface: A car rental firm is based in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDFORDSHIRE is an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a county, an administrative area of the English Midlands.

clue.text: I am kept up by sumo wrestling and heavy metal

indicators.note: kept means held, so the reversed letters are held inside the scrambled word
wrestling means grappling, so the letters of sumo are thrown around
up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A sumo wrestler is held up by a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' and 'kept' put the turned contraction inside the 'wrestling' of sumo. 'Heavy metal' looks like music but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, a very heavy metal.

clue.text: At first chaos follows, with European out for the count

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of chaos is taken
out means the letter for European is dropped

parts.note: ensues means follows

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when a European boxer is knocked out for the count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes an E from ENSUES, leaving ENSUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official counting of the population.

clue.text: Stumped tubby husband, holding record by Queen is not original pop?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the record sits within the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the cricket abbreviation for stumped
tubby means fat
an EP is an extended-play record
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A record by the band Queen leaves a fat man puzzled, wondering whether it is really pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the record inside the stumped-tubby-husband string. 'Pop' is a father, and one who is not the original is a replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal word for dad; a mother's later husband is a replacement dad.

clue.text: Cobbler initially needs some wood to make it

definitions.text: Cobbler initially needs some wood to make it

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of cobbler is taken

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A shoemaker needs a piece of wood to make a wooden shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden-soled shoe, which a cobbler would indeed make from a block of wood.

clue.text: Boss is in the soup — not good

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: gumbo is a thick Louisiana soup

explanation.surface: The boss is in trouble, which is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager; it is the raised centre of a shield. 'In the soup' means in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical synonym: the raised knob at the centre of a shield.

clue.text: To dedicate novel is nicer, having penned book

indicators.note: having penned means enclosing, as a pen holds animals, so the book letter goes inside
novel means new, so these letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: An author dedicating a novel finds it nicer to have written a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ISNICER into INSCRIE; 'having penned' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a dedication in a book is a way to mark it to someone.

clue.text: Little son needs to sponge neck

parts.note: S is the short form of son
to sponge off someone is to mooch, to scrounge

explanation.surface: A small boy must wash his neck with a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is not the body part but the verb meaning to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for kissing and cuddling amorously.

clue.text: Statement about Bond's organisation's bad behaviour

parts.note: M is the head of MI6, James Bond's secret service, in the novels and films
a statement about the boss M would be that he is chief

explanation.surface: A report about Bond's spy agency describes its misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence, 'M is chief' is a statement about Bond's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: naughty, troublesome conduct, especially by children.

clue.text: Quangos siphoned a certain amount off, creating scandal

indicators.note: a certain amount means only part of the words is taken, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Public bodies skimmed off funds, causing a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: QUANGOs are semi-independent British public bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk about other people's affairs, the stuff of scandal.
